entries.title: Explainers reference by @paji_a
entries.author: paji_a
entries.prompt_text: Stage {HISTORIC_BATTLE} as a cinematic 3D overhead battle map in a single HTML file with three.js. Sculpt the real terrain with hills, rivers and roads, place each army as blocks of banner-carrying troops colored by side, and play the day in phases: sweeping arrows for advances, flank attacks and turning points, drifting morning fog, and a camera that glides between key moments. Add captions with time of day and commander names, plus pause, scrub and orbit controls, and keep it running well on a phone.

entries.title: Explainers reference by @DotCSV
entries.author: DotCSV
entries.prompt_text: Animate a tiny neural network learning to recognize handwritten digits, in crisp pixel art on a black background. A 28×28 input grid sketches a digit, three hidden layers of round nodes and thin connection lines glow as activations pass through, and output labels 0 to 9 light up by confidence. Train a real small network in JavaScript so predictions visibly improve while a loss readout falls. Use p5.js at low resolution scaled up without smoothing, and render one minute at 1920×1080 with ffmpeg.

entries.title: Explainers reference by @uchita_success
entries.author: uchita_success
entries.prompt_text: Turn {REPORT_OR_DATA} into a slide deck that feels alive, built as one HTML file. Each slide opens with a headline claim while key figures count up and charts draw themselves in. Every number gets a small control that expands the sources and arithmetic behind it, and sliders for the main assumptions recalculate figures and charts instantly. Use restrained corporate typography, a single teal accent, keyboard navigation and smooth slide transitions. Finish by recording a 30-second walkthrough at 1920×1080 with headless Chrome and ffmpeg.

entries.title: Explainers reference by @AndrewOnXYZ
entries.author: AndrewOnXYZ
entries.prompt_text: Explain {AI_RISK_TOPIC} in a five-minute animated film with the weight of a science documentary: letterboxed 2.39:1 frames, near-black space, colossal silhouetted structures caught by one hard light, and slow, deliberate camera moves. Build the scenes in three.js, carry the argument with calm TTS narration and sparse on-screen lines, and score it with a low synthesized drone that swells at key turns. Render frames with headless Chrome at 1920×1080, 30 fps, and encode with ffmpeg.

entries.title: Explainers reference by @deedydas
entries.author: deedydas
entries.prompt_text: Turn the research paper at {PAPER_PDF} into an eight-minute explainer in the style of 3Blue1Brown, built with Manim. Read the paper closely, then write a narration that builds intuition before any formula, split into scenes for the problem, the core idea, the method step by step, the results and the open questions. Animate diagrams, equations and plots on a dark background with smooth transforms, voice the script with a calm TTS narrator, sync each animation to its sentence, and render 1920×1080 at 60 fps.

entries.title: Explainers reference by @mustafaakin
entries.author: mustafaakin
entries.prompt_text: Direct a 70-second cinematic explainer about {PROJECT} ({WHAT_IT_DOES}) that feels like a brooding Christopher Nolan teaser. Frame everything in 2.39:1 letterbox with film grain and vignette, use slow push-ins on abstract three.js visuals such as logic gates lighting up and bits flowing through circuitry, and reveal the key numbers ({KEY_STATS}) one stark white title card at a time. Score it in code with a ticking clock, a rising Shepard tone and heavy brass hits, then render with headless Chrome and ffmpeg at 1920×1080.

entries.title: Explainers reference by @drecamz
entries.author: drecamz
entries.prompt_text: Produce a 60-second faceless YouTube explainer about {TOPIC} in Remotion. Write a tight script with a hook in the first five seconds, voice it with a TTS narrator, and illustrate every line with clean flat motion graphics: mock chat windows that type out answers, icons, labels and simple charts floating over desaturated photo textures. Stick to a light palette with one purple accent, cut on the narration beats, add soft whooshes and a quiet music bed composed in code, and render at 1280×720, 30 fps, plus a matching thumbnail.

entries.author: lucian__03
entries.prompt_text: Zoom from the rows of racks in an AI data center down to a single silicon atom in one continuous shot, built in one HTML file with three.js. Fly into a rack, slide out a server, take an Nvidia Blackwell GPU board apart piece by piece, then descend through the chip package, the metal wiring layers and a field of transistors to the crystal lattice. Keep a field-of-view scale readout in meters on screen, light it like a clean industrial render, and record 50 seconds at 1920×1080.

entries.title: Explainers reference by @HindolSengupta
entries.author: HindolSengupta
entries.prompt_text: Tell the story of five thousand years of Indian thought about the divine as a four-minute documentary explainer. Move from Indus Valley seals and Vedic hymns through the Upanishads, the epics, temple traditions, bhakti poets, Sufi and Sikh voices to the present, with even-handed, respectful narration. Style it like a quiet museum exhibition: warm parchment tones, refined serif titles with Devanagari lines, slow fades, maps, timelines and line drawings. Voice it with TTS over a soft drone composed in code, and build it in Remotion at 1920×1080.

entries.prompt_text: Tell the story of {HISTORICAL_EVENT} in a 60-second narrated video styled like a Japanese gold-leaf folding screen. Build every scene in code in one HTML file: bands of golden cloud, ink-drawn figures and castles, animated maps, flames and brush-lettered title cards, with slow pans and glowing transitions. Render deterministic frames with headless Chrome and combine them with the narration in ffmpeg at 1920×1080.

entries.title: Explainers reference by @addyosmani
entries.author: addyosmani
entries.prompt_text: Explain what happens after you type a URL in a 40-second hand-drawn explainer, with every frame drawn in JavaScript on a canvas. A friendly robot mascot walks through each stage: DNS lookup, TCP and TLS handshakes, the HTTP request, parsing HTML into the DOM, styling, layout, paint and compositing, with a step counter in the corner. Use wobbly pencil outlines, paper grain and pastel stripes. Render frames deterministically with headless Chrome, add light sound effects, and encode 1920×1080 at 30 fps with ffmpeg.

entries.prompt_text: Turn {HOME_PROJECT} into an interactive 3D instruction manual in one HTML file with three.js. Below the model, list the parts with icons and quantities, the estimated time and a short intro, with Back and Start buttons to step through. entries.title: Explainers reference by @JaneCazneau
entries.author: JaneCazneau
entries.prompt_text: Recreate how {HISTORICAL_SOUND} really sounded in a 40-second audio history explainer, starting from the archival recording at {AUDIO_FILE}. In Python, clean the recording, shift the voice to sound younger, then layer many varied copies with offsets in timing, pitch and distance to grow it from one voice to a crowd of thousands, updating the spectrogram and caption at each step. Render 1920×1080 with ffmpeg.

entries.title: Explainers reference by @jmitani
entries.author: jmitani
entries.prompt_text: Trace 60 years of 3D computer graphics in a 15-second vertical video by rendering the Utah teapot the way each era would have. Write your own small software renderer in Python with NumPy, no 3D libraries, and step through wireframe, hidden-surface removal, flat and Gouraud shading, Phong highlights, texture mapping, ray-traced reflections and soft global illumination. Label every stage with its year and technique above a glowing timeline and encode 1080×1920 at 30 fps with ffmpeg.

entries.prompt_text: Chart the Mongol conquests from 1206 to 1294 as an animated, interactive atlas in one HTML file, using D3 or MapLibre over a dark, antique-toned basemap. entries.prompt_text: Illustrate {TOPIC} in a 50-second biology animation drawn like colored-pencil textbook plates on warm, grainy paper, opening on a single cell with its nucleus and organelles. entries.title: Explainers reference by @tommy_love123
entries.author: tommy_love123
entries.prompt_text: Teach stochastic differential equations in an 8-minute Manim video. Start with a coin-flip random walk, shrink the steps until it becomes Brownian motion, then add drift and noise to arrive at dX = μ dt + σ dW. Show many sample paths fanning out with their spreading distribution, walk through the Euler–Maruyama method step by step, and finish with stock prices as an application. Use a dark background, calm pacing, a TTS voiceover with subtitles in {LANGUAGE}, and render at 1920×1080.
